title: Senior Security Engineer, Security Research

sections.minimum_qualifications:
- Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience.
- 5 years of experience with reverse engineering.
- Experience with vulnerability and exploitation.
- Experience with technical writing.
sections.preferred_qualifications:
- Track record of excellent published security research.
- Ability to demonstrate significant depth of understanding in one or more vulnerability research security fields.
- Excellent team-work, organizational and communication skills.
sections.about:
Our Security team works to create and maintain the safest operating environment for Google's users and developers. Security Engineers work with network equipment and actively monitor our systems for attacks and intrusions. In this role, you will also work with software engineers to proactively identify and fix security flaws and vulnerabilities.
Project Zero is a vendor-agnostic security research team housed within Google. The team aims to improve user security and increase the cost of targeted attacks by conducting industry leading security research.
Our mission is to make zero-day exploits hard. Project Zero team members perform vulnerability research on security-critical software, and use their research results to drive industry-wide defensive improvements.
We build tooling to scale security research, and create new methodologies for discovering high impact security vulnerabilities. We also use in-house exploit development to provide relevant and actionable guidance for long-term defenses and mitigations, and engage in non-technical work such as driving improvements to industry security processes and best practices.
Individual pay is determined by factors including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.
Germany: €128000 - €131000 (EUR) + 15% bonus target + equity + benefits
Learn more about benefits at Google.
sections.responsibilities:
- Conduct vulnerability research and exploit development, specifically in (but not limited to) iOS, MacOS and XNU.
- Create tools and infrastructure that enables the team to scale up our research efforts.
- Engage the wider defensive community by publishing your results.
- Work with other security engineers on the analysis of, and response to vulnerabilities reported by other parties
